title: Determination of Podocyte Number and Density in Rodent Glomeruli
author: Frank Brosius
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8eyhtfw
materials: To measure the glomerular area using Metamorph software, camera and microscope should be calibrated and values should be loaded into Metamorph program before outlining the glomerular tuft area. Click on the desktop icon (Metamorph software icon) to open the Metamorph program, and then open the images. From the menu bar, select Measure , then select Calibrate Distance . A calibration window will appear. Highlight the 40x calibration and then click Apply . Use Polygon tool from menu bar for outlining the glomerular tuft area. From the menu bar, select Measure and then Region Measurement to obtain the measurement of the glomerular tuft area.

steps.title: Fix and section kidneys
steps.instruction: Perfuse mouse or rat kidneys with 2 % paraformaldehyde or PLP, embed in paraffin, and cut longitudinal sections at 3 µm and 9 µm thickness; verify the actual thickness generated by the cryotome before proceeding.

steps.title: Immunostain sections for WT‑1
steps.instruction: Stain the sections with WT‑1 antibody using conventional immunoperoxidase procedures as described in the WT‑1 Staining Protocol for podocytes.

steps.title: Capture whole cortical images
steps.instruction: Take photographs of the entire cortical area at 40× magnification using a Spot Advanced Software‑compatible camera (or similar).

steps.title: Photograph 50 glomerular sections
steps.instruction: Systematically photograph 50 consecutive glomerular cross‑sections per animal, moving from outer cortex to inner cortex and back across the slide to sample all cortical regions equally; use phase‑contrast illumination to render WT‑1‑positive podocyte nuclei as bright golden objects.

steps.title: Measure area and count podocytes
steps.instruction: Using Metamorph Image Analysis Software, measure the glomerular tuft area and manually count WT‑1‑positive podocyte nuclei in the 50 sequential glomerular sections for each thickness (3 µm and 9 µm).

steps.title: Apply size cut‑off for nuclei
steps.instruction: To exclude artifacts, choose Measure → Manually Count Objects, select size number 6, and count only objects whose size fits within the nuclear profile; discard any WT‑1‑positive objects larger than the size 6 threshold.

steps.title: Calculate podocyte density and volume
steps.instruction:
Perform the following calculations using the data from the 100 cross‑sections (50 per thickness):
1. Compute the average podocyte number (P) and average glomerular area (GA) for each thickness.
2. Calculate P/GA for each thickness.
3. Determine Δ(P/GA) = (P/GA)_9µm – (P/GA)_3µm, which corresponds to the actual section‑thickness difference (~6 µm).
4. Compute average glomerular volume per podocyte (GV/P) = 6.3 µm / Δ(P/GA).
5. Estimate glomerular radius for each thickness: R = √(GA/π).
6. Obtain average radius R_av, then maximum radius R_max = (4 R_av)/π.
7. Calculate average glomerular volume: GV = (4/3) π (R_max)³.
8. Derive podocyte number per glomerulus: P_glom = GV / (GV/P).
